name: Max Payne
blurb: A grieving cop, a blizzard, and a city that answers questions with gunfire.
description: Remedy's noir shooter turned slow motion into a signature and a metaphor: a man moving through a nightmare at half speed. The comic-panel storytelling, winter New York, and Valkyr conspiracy gave Rockstar's catalog one of its coldest, most stylish voices.

name: Manhunt
blurb: A surveillance-state nightmare staged as a snuff film, with the player as the audience.
description: Manhunt is Rockstar at its most confrontational: stealth, execution, and a camera that never lets you forget you are watching. Its critique of violence and spectatorship is uncomfortable by design, and it remains the studio's darkest experiment.

name: Midnight Club
blurb: Illegal street racing, city lights, and a love of speed before the open-world boom.
description: Midnight Club brought Rockstar's sense of place to racing: real-city inspiration, night-time streets, and a culture of custom cars and rival crews. It is the bridge between arcade racing and the studio's later city-building instincts.

name: L.A. Noire
blurb: A detective story where faces are evidence.
description: Team Bondi and Rockstar built a 1947 Los Angeles of interrogations, traffic desks, and performance-captured faces. The city is warm and corrupt, and the truth is usually behind a lie.
